title: Andrew Brandt on MLB Salary Cap Fight as World Series Begins
title_cn: Andrew Brandt on MLB Salary Cap Fight as World Series Begins
summary: Andrew Brandt says the Brewers and Rays reaching the World Series—despite ranking 19th and 26th in payroll, respectively—shows how strong management, scouting and player development can compete with high spending. He calls the matchup evidence for the players’ union that success is possible without a salary cap, while cautioning that owners may dismiss it as an unsustainable exception: smaller-market teams have little margin for error and can lose players to wealthier clubs in free agency. title: Oncologists Cheer Melanoma Data
title_cn: Oncologists Cheer Melanoma Data
summary:
Leaked data from Moderna and Merck's highly anticipated melanoma vaccine trial has led to a rare disconnect between doctors, who celebrated the result, and Wall Street, which sold off the stocks.
Normally results of such pivotal drug studies are binary, with doctors, patients and investors all learning whether a novel medicine will make a meaningful difference in people’s lives and forming the same conclusion. Instead, as reports leaked out on social media about the findings of the melanoma shot — days before the carefully scripted presentation planned for thousands of oncologists gathered in Madrid for the European Society for Medical Oncology meeting — realities diverged.  Madison Muller, Bloomberg News Healthcare Reporter, reports.   (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gutierrez: US Has Gone Too Far With Tariffs
title_cn: Gutierrez: US Has Gone Too Far With Tariffs
summary: Carlos Gutierrez, former Commerce Secretary and CEO of Kellogg and author of Sheer Will, says trade under the Trump administration has become all-encompassing and can be used as part of geopolitical and political negotiations beyond trade itself. Gutierrez says the US has gone too far with tariffs and that easing them could help reduce inflationary pressure on American consumers. Gutierrez says the US has the infrastructure and capabilities to be a strong exporter, but should focus on high-value industries rather than making consumers pay more to bring back lower-value production. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gen. Hodges (Ret.) Says Trump Actions Help Russia's War
title_cn: Gen. Hodges (Ret.) Says Trump Actions Help Russia's War
summary: Gen. Ben Hodges (Ret.) says restrictions on Starlink service have dealt a significant blow to Ukraine's counter-drone capabilities and disrupted an early-warning system for incoming ballistic missiles. Hodges says it is bizarre for President Donald Trump to defend Elon Musk as a "good person" who would not do anything wrong, pointing to Trump's praise of Vladimir Putin and Kim Jong Un and comments from a Trump negotiator calling Putin a humanitarian. Hodges says he applauds first lady Melania Trump's role in helping secure relief for Ukrainian civilians, but says it represents only a small fraction of the suffering caused by Russia's war. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
